privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.intro: Restock is a free, open-source app that helps you spend less on groceries. It isn't here to take advantage of you. There's no account, no advertising, no analytics and no tracking, and the people who make Restock never receive your data, except feedback you choose to send them and the shelf prices your phone reads from the shops, if you leave Shared prices on (both below). All the code is public, so anyone can check that this is true.
summary: Everything you put in Restock stays on your phone.
No account, no ads, no analytics, no tracking.
Permissions are only used for the feature that asks for them, and only when you use it.
Costco is off until you pick it with your shops. Its website terms ask people not to collect its listings, so Restock shows you a notice first and only looks when you search.

The app talks directly to the shops and a few open services. It sends things to us only for feedback you send and, with Shared prices on, the shelf prices it reads from the shops, in return for the shared price history it downloads from GitHub.

If you turn on sync, your household's phones share your Restock data straight with each other over your Wi-Fi, encrypted, or through a folder you pick, sealed so only your phones can read it. It never goes through us.

If you run your own Restock server, it keeps what your phones share with it, at your home. It only contacts the shops if you turn on "Let the web page search the shops", and only when someone presses Search.

"Shared prices" is on unless you turn it off: your phone downloads the shared price history, so new items are judged from day one, and shares the shelf prices it reads from Coles, Woolworths, Aldi and Costco (shop, product, price, the day). They're published openly on GitHub, free, and never sold. Never anything you type in, and nothing about you.
Settings → Your data works out what you spend from what you tick off. It stays on your phone, or with your own Restock server, it goes to your server unless you turn that off. It never comes to us.
Feedback reaches us only when you press Send, with diagnostics unless you turn them off, and your email only if you type it.

sections.title: What stays on your phone
body: Your pantry, Keg and Health items, shopping lists, the shops you've picked or added yourself, price history, loyalty and gift cards (barcodes, card numbers, PINs, balances, expiry dates and photos), household name, categories and settings are stored in a database on your phone. They never leave it unless you export a backup, turn on sync, which copies them to the other phones in your household (see Sync between your phones), or connect your own Home Assistant, which gets your groceries list.

Gift cards are never synced or shared, never sent to a Restock server, and never in the spreadsheet or export files from the server. They leave your phone only in your own backups: in a backup you export when you tick Cards, and in automatic backups only when they're locked with a password. Cards you add in the server's web page are kept only in that browser, apart for each server and household, so another household signing in there never sees them. Signing out asks whether to keep them, and if a sign-out never asked (the server ended the session, say), the next sign-in to another household asks.
Uninstalling Restock, or clearing its storage in Android settings, deletes all of it.

"Erase everything and start fresh" in Settings deletes all of it from this phone too. It also signs you out of any shop you signed in to inside Restock, and clears the files Restock exported (its own copies of the backups, spreadsheets and diagnostics files it handed to Android's share menu). Files you already saved or sent somewhere else stay where you put them.

Price history is kept for as long as you choose in Settings → Prices and deals (How far back Restock looks): 8 weeks unless you change it, 6 months or 12 months. Older prices are deleted from the phone automatically.

What you spend (Settings → Your data) is worked out on your phone from the lines you tick off your shopping list: each tick, its shop, the price and the day. It isn't synced to your other phones and is never in a backup. With your own Restock server, your phone also sends it to your server, unless you turn off Share my spending with the server (Settings → Sync and backups): what it worked out before it joined goes once, and then Your data shows your household's figures from your server. It never goes to us. Erase everything deletes it from the phone.

Receipts you keep (the photo, shop, date, total and the words read off it) are stored inside Restock's own storage, not in your phone's photo gallery. They're deleted automatically after the time you choose, counted from the day you scanned each one: 3 months unless you change it, or kept until you delete them. Pinned receipts are kept.
If you turn on the Keg tab, Restock asks you to confirm you're 18 or over. That answer is kept only on your phone, like everything else.

sections.title: What we collect
body: Only feedback you send, and the shop prices Shared prices sends (turn it off in Settings → Privacy and sharing). Restock has no sign-in, no crash reporting, no analytics and no advertising. We can't see who you are, what you buy or where you live. Shared prices does tell us which products a phone's searches and price checks showed, with a random number for that install (so phones can be told apart) and never your name, account, branch, list or anything you typed. Feedback you send from Settings → Send feedback comes to us too (see Feedback).

sections.title: Permissions and what they're for
body: Internet: to look up prices and stock, and for the services listed below.

Camera: to scan barcodes and QR codes, and to photograph a receipt or the front of a pack if you use those. It's only on while you're using it. Barcode and pack pictures are read on your phone and not kept; receipt photos are kept only inside Restock, for as long as you choose. Nothing is sent anywhere.

Approximate location: only when you tap "Use my location" to find nearby supermarkets, bottle shops or chemists. Restock asks Android once, uses the result to look up shops, and keeps only the area name and position on your phone. It never tracks you in the background, and never asks for precise location.
Notifications, and alarms & reminders: to tell you about deals and send the reminders you choose. They're made on your phone.
Vibration: a small buzz when you add something to your list.

Wi-Fi network discovery, staying ready in the background, and starting after a restart: only if you turn on sync. Restock uses them to find your household's other phones on your Wi-Fi and to sync with them while it's closed. While it's ready to sync, Android shows a quiet notification. Restock may also ask to be left out of Android's battery saving, so sync keeps working while it's closed.

Running in the background and keeping the phone awake: only while a search test you started in Diagnostics is running, so it can carry on with the screen off. A notification shows how far it's got, with a Stop button.
Every permission is optional. Turn any of them off in Android settings and the rest of the app keeps working.

Photos: there's no photos permission. If you import a barcode from a picture, Android's photo picker hands Restock only the one picture you choose. It's read on your phone to find the code and isn't kept.

sections.title: Services the app talks to, straight from your phone
body: The shops you pick (Coles, Woolworths and Aldi, and any bottle shops, chemists or shop websites you add): when you search, add an item, check prices or open a product's details, your phone asks that shop's website for product names, prices and stock, just like visiting the site. Searches only go to the shops on the tab you're using, so a grocery search never goes to a bottle shop or chemist. The shop sees an ordinary visit from your phone's internet connection, and may set its usual cookies. Sometimes Restock opens the shop's website in a hidden built-in browser to do this; the shop's own website code, including its analytics, runs there as it would in any browser. Each shop's own privacy policy applies to these visits.

Your Woolworths account, only if you sign in to it inside Restock: you sign in on Woolworths' own page in Restock's built-in browser, so your email and password go to Woolworths, never to Restock. Restock then asks Woolworths' website for your branch's prices and stock, and can add items to your trolley, the way the website does. Restock keeps only whether you're signed in and which branch your account uses. Stop using it any time in Settings → My shops, and sign out on the Woolworths page to end the session there. Your Coles branch number, if you give it, is sent to Coles with each search so the prices and stock are for that branch.

Costco, only if you pick it with your shops (it's off until you do). Read this first: Costco's website terms say automated collection of product listings isn't allowed. Restock only looks when you search, one page at a time. It never checks Costco in the background or with Check now, and never in bulk. Costco may block it or change its pages, so it may stop working. Treat it as a test feature. It's your choice to turn this on, and your responsibility. Prices are Costco's online prices, which include delivery. They can differ from warehouse to warehouse and from the shelf. Restock asks Costco's website from inside its own page in the app, like Woolworths. You can sign in to Costco there for member prices: your password goes to Costco, not Restock. Costco prices are shared and backed up like any shop's, and with Shared prices on, the Costco prices your searches show go to Restock's shared price service too.

Diagnostics recordings, only when you start one: while you add something to a shop's trolley yourself, Restock notes what that shop's own page asks its servers. Sign-in, account, payment and tracking calls are left out, and names, emails, phone numbers, addresses, card and member numbers, and the values in web addresses (such as search words) are blanked. The recording stays on your phone unless you choose to share it.

Search test, "Send search details" and "Wrong results?" files, only when you make one: the words searched and what the shops sent back for them, saved in a file on your phone. Nothing from your pantry, lists or settings is in it, and "Send search details" searches the shop's website, not your branch. A shop's answer can still be about you: if you're signed in to Woolworths inside Restock, Woolworths answers for your account (its branch's prices and stock, and possibly what's in your trolley), so check the file before you share it. It goes nowhere unless you choose to share it.

Open Food Facts, Open Beauty Facts and Open Products Facts (openfoodfacts.org, openbeautyfacts.org and openproductsfacts.org), the Open Food Facts project's free, open product databases: when you scan a barcode or open a product's details, the barcode number is sent to look up the product's name, ingredients, allergens and nutrition. Restock asks the one most likely to know it first (Open Beauty Facts on the Health tab, for example), and the others only if it doesn't. Nothing else is sent.

Barcodes at the supermarkets: if those databases don't know a barcode well enough, Restock may search Woolworths and Coles for it to find the product's name, but only the ones you've switched on, and without your sign-in. It first asks the shop directly from your phone, with a separate set of cookies kept only in your phone's memory and deleted when Restock closes or when you use Erase everything, never the cookies of Restock's in-app browser. If the shop turns that away and you're not signed in to that shop in Restock, Restock may ask through its in-app browser instead, which then has no account of yours to send. If you are signed in to that shop in Restock, it never does: that shop is simply skipped for that scan. As with any website, the shop sees the barcode and your phone's internet address. A shop you've switched off is never asked.

OpenStreetMap (Nominatim at nominatim.openstreetmap.org, and the Overpass map servers overpass-api.de and overpass.private.coffee): when you look for nearby shops, the suburb or postcode you type, or your approximate position rounded to about 100 metres, is sent to find the closest supermarkets, bottle shops or chemists. The Overpass servers are asked one at a time: the second only if the first doesn't answer. Nothing else is sent.

The official recall lists (Food Standards Australia New Zealand, Product Safety Australia and the Therapeutic Goods Administration), while recall alerts are on: once a day, and when you tap Check now, Restock downloads their public lists of recent recalls, the same for everyone. Matching them against your items, list and receipts happens on your phone; nothing about you is sent.

No service, for receipts: the receipt reader (Tesseract, open-source text recognition, and its English model) is built into Restock since version 0.7.4, so nothing is downloaded. Receipts are read on your phone and never sent anywhere.
Store catalogue links open in your phone's web browser, under that website's own policy.

GitHub (raw.githubusercontent.com, the restock-prices project), while Shared prices is on (it's on unless you turn it off, in setup or Settings → Privacy and sharing). restock-prices is Restock's own collection of Coles, Woolworths, Aldi and Costco shelf prices: Restock's collector every Thursday, and the prices phones send back, added each night. It's published openly on GitHub. Restock downloads only the files for the shops you picked, for how far back you chose (8 weeks, 6 months or 12 months), weekly after the Thursday collection or every day if you choose. They're the same files for everyone, and nothing about you or what you track is sent to get them. Phones don't download from hotprices.org; the collector uses it.

Your own restock-prices collector, only on a phone you set up as a price helper (Settings → Advanced → Price helper phone). That phone searches Coles and Woolworths for everyday things while it charges, and sends the products and shelf prices it found, plus the newest prices of your household's own Coles and Woolworths products, to the collector address you type in, with the key you type in. Nothing about you, your list, cards or receipts is sent. The collector publishes them in restock-prices, without saying where they came from.

Restock's shared price service (restock-prices.plenty.family/share/prices, run by the people who make Restock), while Shared prices is on (it's on unless you turn it off). A few minutes after a search, and after background price checks, your phone sends what Coles, Woolworths, Aldi and Costco's websites showed: for each product, the shop, its product number, name, brand, size, barcode and picture link, the price with any "was" price, special, member price or multi-buy, and the day. With it goes a random number made for this install, so the service can tell phones apart and limit how much one sends, and, like any website, your internet address, used for the same limit and never written down. Never prices you typed in or changed, products from shops you added, sample items, your list, pantry, cards, branch, location, account or anything about you. The service checks each price, keeps its own collector's readings first, and publishes the prices in restock-prices (see GitHub, above), without saying which phone they came from. The web page on a Restock server never sends any.

Restock's feedback inbox (restock-prices.plenty.family, run by the people who make Restock), only when you press Send in Settings → Send feedback, on the phone or your Restock server's web page. It gets what kind of feedback it is and your message, any screenshots you attach, your email only if you type one, Restock's version and the kind of device. Unless you turn Attach diagnostics off, it also gets diagnostics: your settings with passwords, keys, tokens, addresses, branches and names taken out, recent problems with shops, and how sync and shared prices are doing ("See what's included" shows exactly what). It also gets a random number made for this install, only to limit how much one phone can send in a day, and, like any website, your internet address, used for the same limit and not kept with your message. Your pantry, lists, cards, receipts and prices are never in it. With no connection it waits on your phone and goes the next time Restock opens. Feedback is read only by the people who make Restock, kept on their server for as long as it's useful, and never sold or shared. Ask, from the email you used, and we'll delete yours.

GitHub (github.com), only when you tap Check for updates in Settings, or once a week if you turn on "Tell me when there's an update". Restock asks for the latest release's version number and notes, and if you tap Update, downloads the new APK from there. Nothing about you or what you track is sent.

Home Assistant (your own), only if you connect it in Settings → Sync and backups → Home Assistant. The phone you turn it on on talks straight to your Home Assistant, at the address you give it, and nothing goes through us or anyone else. It sends and reads your groceries list: each line's name and how many, and whether it's ticked off. Nothing else from Restock goes to Home Assistant. The long-lived access token you paste in stays on that phone only, sealed with a key in Android's key store. It's never shown again, synced to your other phones or put in a backup. Restock uses plain http:// only for a Home Assistant on your home network or on Tailscale, and https:// anywhere else. Only one phone in your household does this, and which one it is (just that phone's place in your household, never the address or token) is shared with your household so the others know. Your other phones get the list through your household's sync, as usual.

sections.title: Backups
body: "Export a backup" makes one file with the parts you pick: each tab's items (with or without price history), shopping lists, loyalty cards and gift cards (including their numbers, PINs and photos, only when you tick Cards), receipts (with or without their photos) and settings. You choose where it goes through Android's share menu. If gift cards are in it and you don't set a password, Restock warns you first. Keep it somewhere private, and don't post it publicly.

Automatic backups are off unless you turn them on. When they're on, Restock saves a whole backup into a folder you pick, as often as you choose, and removes its own older automatic backups so only the newest few are kept. Gift cards (their numbers, PINs and photos) are only included when automatic backups are locked with a password; without one they're left out. If that folder is synced by a cloud app, that app's own policy applies to the copies it keeps.

You can lock a backup with a password. The whole file is then encrypted on your phone, and nobody can open it without the password, including us and you if you forget it. Restock doesn't keep the password of a backup you export. The password for automatic backups, if you set one, is kept on your phone only and never put in a backup.

Just before a new version of Restock first opens, it saves a backup (without receipt photos) inside the app, so an update that changed something it shouldn't have can be undone. The last two are kept. If you use automatic backups, a copy also goes into that folder, locked if they are.
"Export as spreadsheets" makes CSV files of your pantry, shopping list and price history, and hands them to Android's share menu. Where they go is up to you.

With "Shared prices" on (the default), a backup that includes price history also has a "shared prices" part: products and their prices only, for the items in that backup, nothing about you (see Sharing prices). Your spending record (Your data) is never in a backup.

sections.title: Sync between your phones
body: Local sync is off unless you turn it on (Settings → Sync and backups). When it's on, the phones in your household send each other the parts you choose to share (groceries, Keg and Health: their items, shopping list, prices, categories and alert settings), and loyalty card numbers if you choose to share them, directly over your own Wi-Fi. Parts you don't share stay on your phone. On the Wi-Fi, nothing goes through the internet or any server. Wi-Fi sync is its own option: on a Restock server it stays off until you set it up, and nothing is advertised on your network until then. Gift cards are never shared. The makers of Restock never see any of it.

Everything sent between the phones is encrypted with a key made on the phone that started the household (the owner phone). The key is never shown or put in a code: a phone joins by scanning a one-time code that works once and only for 10 minutes, and is then given the key over the encrypted link. A phone or computer without the key can't read what's sent or join in. When the owner removes a phone, the household's key changes so that phone can't sync again.
Each phone keeps its own copy. Stopping sync on a phone keeps what it has; to remove the household's things from a phone, delete them or uninstall Restock there.

Sync away from home is off unless you set it up: through your Nextcloud, another WebDAV server, or a folder on your phone that an app like Syncthing keeps the same. Each phone then writes one file there with the household's list, pantry, categories and alert settings, its shared loyalty cards if you chose to share them, and its kept receipts if the household shares them, sealed with the household's key so only your phones can read it. Prices and photos aren't included. If you sign in to Nextcloud, Nextcloud gives Restock a password of its own, so your own password never reaches Restock, and Restock asks Nextcloud to delete it when it stops using it. A WebDAV password you type in stays on your phone only. Restock only connects to a server over https, unless the server is on your home network or on Tailscale. Whoever stores the folder can see that the files are there, their size and when they change, but not what's in them. When the owner removes a phone, the owner also leaves the new key in the folder, sealed separately for each remaining phone.

The owner phone has a recovery key: 32 letters and numbers for you to keep somewhere safe. If the owner phone is lost, another phone in the household can take over as the owner with it. The other phones keep a sealed copy of what that needs, which only the recovery key opens. The key itself is only shown on the owner phone, after its screen lock. Restock never sends it anywhere, and we can't recover it for you.

Receipts are only shared if the owner phone turns on "Share receipts with the household" (it's off unless you do). Their details then go to the other phones like the rest of the household's things, for the tabs each phone shares, and their photos only go directly between the phones over your Wi-Fi. Phones only look for each other on Wi-Fi or a network cable, never over mobile data.

The household's keys, the secrets a takeover needs and any sync server password are sealed on each phone with a key kept in Android's key store. Each phone keeps a short record of which changes the others have seen, so it can tidy away old deletes after 90 days once every phone has them.

From 0.9.2, phones can also sync through a Restock server you run yourself (Settings → Sync and backups → Restock server), for example a Docker container on your own NAS or an app in Home Assistant. From 0.9.4 the server is the household: you name it on its web page and add each phone there with a one-time code. Each phone makes its own key for the server, which keeps only the public half, and chooses what it shares: groceries (the pantry, the shopping list and the General list) always, and Keg, Health, receipts and loyalty cards only if you turn them on. What a phone shares goes to the server sealed, as with folder sync, so it's encrypted on the way even over plain http. The server holds the household's key and keeps what the phones share in its own database, so it can read it: that's what lets it sync around the clock, keep your history, show it on your computer and run Home Assistant. If a phone shares its loyalty cards, their numbers pass through the server in that phone's sealed file, but the server's database keeps only the cards' names. The server keeps what's shared until you delete it on its web page (Data → Manage data), or for as long as you choose with Auto delete, which is off on a new server unless you turn it on. Removing a phone doesn't delete what that phone shared, and the server keeps a log of which phone or browser did what. From 0.9.5 it also notes each thing ticked off the shopping list (what it was, how many, the price, the shop and the day) to show your spending in its Data tab. With a Restock server, Home Assistant is set up on the server instead of a phone: the server keeps the token and syncs your groceries list with your Home Assistant.

The server also serves Restock for your computer's browser. You sign in with the server's user name and passphrase, or by scanning the page's code with a phone. Your passphrase isn't sent to the server: the browser proves it knows it. The browser keeps a copy of the household's things in its storage for that site until you sign out. That's also how Restock works on an iPhone's home screen: the copy (and the older prices you looked at) lets your lists, pantry and cards open with no signal, and signing out takes it off. The Data tab can download your household's data as a spreadsheet, CSV files or a full export file; they hold your list, pantry, prices and spending (never loyalty or gift card numbers, PINs, receipt text or photos, keys or passwords), so keep them private. The Data tab can also import products and prices from a file you choose: it adds them without replacing anything, and refuses files with card numbers, PINs, passwords, keys or receipts in them. Your data lives on your server, and you're responsible for keeping it updated, backed up and secure; keep its data folder and backups private, because they hold your household's data. The makers of Restock never see any of it.

Let the web page search the shops is a setting on your Restock server, off unless you turn it on. When it's on and someone presses Search on the server's web page, the server asks the built-in shops on that tab for the words typed, the same way a phone does, so the shops see your server's internet address instead of a phone's. The server only does this when someone presses Search: nothing runs in the background, no shop sign-ins are used or kept, and shops you added yourself are never asked. Its log notes that a search happened, by which browser, on which tab and how each shop answered, but never what was searched for. Each shop's own privacy policy applies to these visits.

From 0.9.3, some settings are the household's: which shops each shared tab uses, Shop around, the alert level new items start with, recall alerts, the shopping list's cheapest and the order of products. They travel with the household's other shared things (over the Wi-Fi, through the folder and through a Restock server), sealed the same way, and anyone in the household can change them. So do the words you've told Restock to always use for one of your pantry items ("Always use this for milk"), the lines you've chosen to keep as just words, and which phone syncs with Home Assistant. Your branches and branch numbers, your area and everything else stay on your phone. On a Restock server, each phone's file also carries a short summary of that phone's own settings for the web app to show: its Restock version, how often it checks prices and when it last did, which notifications are on, whether it's signed in to Woolworths or Coles (yes or no only), how many loyalty cards it has (never their numbers), whether automatic backups are on and how often (never the folder or password), how long it keeps price history, which tabs it takes, how it syncs away from home (never where), whether Home Assistant is on and which list (never the address or token), its theme and text size, and whether receipts, shared prices and update checks are on. It's sealed on the way like the rest.

sections.title: Sharing prices
body: Shared prices is a free, open price list anyone can use: what things cost at Coles, Woolworths, Aldi and Costco, and when. It's published openly on GitHub (github.com/d-plenty/restock-prices), from Restock's own collector and the prices phones send back. It only ever carries prices and products read from the shops, never anything personal and never anything you typed in. The prices will never be sold.

"Shared prices" is on unless you turn it off (Settings → Privacy and sharing). It's one switch for both halves: your phone downloads the shared history (see GitHub, above), and sends the shelf prices it reads from Coles, Woolworths, Aldi and Costco to restock-prices, Restock's own shared price service (see Services, above), so everyone's day-one prices get better. Turning it off stops both straight away. Turning it back on starts from then: prices read while it was off are never sent. A phone that had sharing off before 0.10.0 stays off until you say otherwise. Prices you type in or change yourself are never sent: they stay on your phone, your household's phones and your own server.

A Restock server's full export file, in an open, documented format, is something else: it's for you, also holds your list, pantry and spending, and stays wherever you save it. A Restock server never sends prices anywhere.

What's in it: for each product Restock has checked at a shop, the shop, its name, brand, size, barcode and the shop's product number, and each price Restock read from the shop with the usual ("was") price, any special or multi-buy, and the day. Only the tabs in that backup are included. The products are the ones you track, but nothing in it links them to you. It never includes who you are, your loyalty or gift cards, your branch or location, your shopping list or what you ticked off, your receipts, or anything you type about yourself. Products and prices you typed in yourself aren't included, and nor are products from shops you added yourself or sample items. Turning Shared prices off leaves it out of your future backups, and nothing is sent.

sections.title: Children
body: Restock isn't made for children and doesn't knowingly collect anything from anyone, of any age.

sections.title: Changes and contact
body: If this policy changes, the new version will be in the app and in the project's source code, with a new date. Questions or concerns? Use Settings → Send feedback, or open an issue on the project's GitHub page: https://github.com/d-plenty/Restock/issues

privacy.tagline: Privacy policy? We collect almost nothing, and we tell you exactly what. Here's the long version.
privacy.outro: If you've read all the way to the bottom: thank you, and also, you might be a tiny bit boring. We say that with love. Go and find something on special.

disclaimer.title: Fine print
summary: Restock isn't connected with any supermarket, bottle shop or chemist.
Prices and stock can be wrong or out of date. Always check the shelf and your receipt.
The app is free and comes with no guarantee.

sections.title: Not affiliated with any shop
body: Restock is an independent project. It isn't made, endorsed or supported by Coles, Woolworths, Aldi, Costco, Dan Murphy's, BWS, Liquorland, Chemist Warehouse, Priceline or any other retailer. Their names belong to them and are used only to say which shop a price came from.

sections.title: Prices and stock can be wrong
body: Prices, specials, member prices and stock come from each shop's website and can be wrong, late or different at your branch or in your state. "In stock" means the shop's online stock, not the shelf near you. Verdicts like "Great deal" or "Wait" are worked out from the price history on your phone and are only a guide. Always check the shelf price and your receipt.

Bottle shop and chemist prices are the online prices on each shop's website. Many chemists and some bottle shops set prices per branch, or show some prices only in the shop, so the price at your local shop can be different, and some shops may show nothing at all.

sections.title: Product information
body: Product names and details, including the ingredients, allergens and nutrition shown under Product details, come from the shops and Open Food Facts. They can be incomplete or out of date, and recipes change. Always check the packet, and never rely on Restock for allergies or dietary needs.
Restock is not medical advice. For medicines, read the label and ask a pharmacist or doctor. Prescription medicines aren't priced by Restock.

sections.title: Alcohol
body: The Keg tab is for adults 18 and over. Restock only compares prices; please drink responsibly. For help, call the National Alcohol and Other Drug Hotline on 1800 250 015.

sections.title: Fair use of shop websites
body: Restock only checks the items you track, one at a time with pauses in between, like a person browsing. Please use it for your own household shopping. A shop may change its website or block requests at any time, and some features may stop working until the app is updated.

If you turn on "Let the web page search the shops" on your own Restock server, it searches only when someone presses Search on its web page, one search at a time, and never in the background. A shop may block searches from a server; then search on a phone.

Costco is the one shop whose website terms say automated collection of product listings isn't allowed, so it's off until you pick it with your shops. Costco's website terms say automated collection of product listings isn't allowed. Restock only looks when you search, one page at a time. It never checks Costco in the background or with Check now, and never in bulk. Costco may block it or change its pages, so it may stop working. Treat it as a test feature. It's your choice to turn this on, and your responsibility. Prices are Costco's online prices, which include delivery. They can differ from warehouse to warehouse and from the shelf. Turning it on is your choice and your responsibility.

sections.title: Data and battery
body: Price checks use a small amount of internet data and battery. Background checks only run on a network connection and when the battery isn't low, and you can turn them off in Settings.

Shared prices, while it's on, downloads the shared price history for your shops once a week after the Thursday collection, or every day if you choose (on Wi-Fi only, unless you change that): roughly 1 MB for 8 weeks to 3 MB for 12 months with all four shops collected, and less for fewer. Settings → Prices and deals shows the size for yours. Sending prices back uses a few kilobytes after each search or price check.

sections.title: No warranty
body: Restock is free, open-source software provided "as is", without warranty of any kind. Its makers aren't responsible for any loss, missed saving or decision made using it. See the licence in the source code for the full terms.

sections.title: Beta software
body: Restock 0.10.0 is a release candidate: everything is in, and it's being tested before 1.0, so things can still change between versions. The Keg and Health tabs are marked Beta: they work the same way as Groceries, they just haven't been tested as thoroughly yet, and they'll keep being tested before they come out of beta. Features under Settings → Advanced are for testing and can change or disappear. If something goes wrong, Settings → Send feedback tells us. Keep a backup of anything you'd hate to lose.
